6689.t: From ὑποκρίνομαι (hupokrínomai, “to play a part on stage”) + -τής (-tḗs).

6616.t: Uncertain. According to Beekes, probably from Pre-Greek.

6654.t: Unknown. Not related to πέσσω (péssō, “to soften, ripen; to cook, dress, bake”).

6672.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ód͏̌d͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ed-ye-, from *h₃ed-. Cognates include Latin odor and Lithuanian úosti.

6607.t: From earlier *ϝέσνυμαι (*wésnumai), from Proto-Indo-European *wes- (“to dress”). Particularly close cognate with Old Armenian զգենում (zgenum, “to dress oneself”).

6608.t: PIE word *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros From Proto-Hellenic *wésperos, from Proto-Indo-European *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros (“evening”). Cognates include Latin vesper, Old Armenian գիշեր (gišer), and Old Church Slavonic вєчєръ (večerŭ).

6676.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wórwos (whence Mycenaean Greek 𐀺𐀺 (wo-wo)), perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *werw- (“to draw, mark out”), with cognates including Latin urvō (“to trace a boundary”).

6600.t: Uhlenbeck and others consider it cognate with Sanskrit रम॑ते (rámate, “to calm down; to enjoy; to have sex with”), Lithuanian rimti (“calm down”), Gothic 𐍂𐌹𐌼𐌹𐍃 (rimis, “tranquility”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rem-; the Greek could then be from a…

6674.t: Nominal derivative from unattested *ὄψ (*óps), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁op-s, a derivative of *h₁epi (“on, near”); delicacies were considered side-dishes and were eaten on top of bread and such.

6605.t: PIE word *swé Apparently from Proto-Hellenic *hwe = *ϝ̔έ (*whé), from Proto-Indo-European *swé (reflexive pronoun).

6601.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wérd͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *wérǵ-ye-, a *ye-present from the root *werǵ-, the same root as ῥέζω (rhézō) and ἔργον (érgon).

6690.t: From the future stem of ὑφοράω (hŭphoráō, “to suspect”) + -εύω (-eúō).

6613.t: According to Beekes from Proto-Indo-European *h₂em- (“to grasp”) and cognate with Latin ānsa (“handle”) and Lithuanian ąsà (“handle”).

6604.t: PIE word *swé From Proto-Indo-European *swet-, from *swé (“self”). Cognate with Proto-Slavic *svatъ (“father of newlyweds”).

6623.t: From Proto-Indo-European *seykʷ- (“to filter”) and cognate with Old English sēon (“to filter”), Russian сцать (scatʹ, “to piss”) and Sanskrit सिञ्चति (siñcáti, “to pour”). Beekes suggests *seyk- as the original root.

6617.t: Unknown. Osthoff and Brugman connected this word to Latin sinō (“to permit, allow”) (assuming cognacy with Latin sēmen (“seed”)), but this is now viewed as impossible.

6640.t: Beekes reconstructs Proto-Indo-European *tḱiH-in (“kite”), connecting the word with Old Armenian ցին (cʻin, “kite”), Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬉𐬥𐬀 (saēna, “a mythical bird”), and Sanskrit श्येन (śyena, “eagle, falcon”).

6624.t: Formation like ἀχλύς (akhlús) and δελφύς (delphús). Identical with Proto-Slavic *jьlъ (“silt; clay”) and Latvian īls (“very dark”).

6631.t: Traditionally derived from εἶμι (eîmĭ, “to be going to go”), which is from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ey-, though most other oxytones in -αμός (-ămós) are substantives (such as ποταμός (potămós)); Beekes suggests it comes from the Attic popular language.

6618.t: From ἡδύς (hēdús, “sweet”) + -ος (-os). Apparently originally an Aeolic form due to the loss of /h/.

6633.t: Per Schwyzer and Frisk, probably from an unattested noun *ἱδρυ- (*hidru-), a derivative in -ρ- (-r-) (comparing ἕδρα (hédra, “seat”)) of Proto-Indo-European *sed- (“to sit; settle”), also seen in ἕζομαι (hézomai, “to sit”) and ἵζω (hízō, “to sit, seat,…

6668.t: From relative ὅς (hós) (or from its stem) + πηνίκα (pēníka). Compare ἡνίκα (hēníka).

6627.t: From ἰσο- (iso-, “equal, equivalent”) + δύναμις (dŭ́nămĭs, “force, power, strength, authority, value, meaning”) + -ος (-os, suffix forming second-declension compound adjectives).

6658.t: It is widely agreed that the initial syllable contains a zero grade s-stem from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ed-. Compare Ancient Greek ὄζω (ózō).

6622.t: From ἴδιος (ĭ́dĭos, “one’s own; peculiar”) + -της (-tēs, abstract noun suffix).
